findings.note: Help text is inconsistent for the new top-level command: `metareview fsm` is listed in the Usage block (main.go:37) but is absent from the `Commands:` list (main.go:55-67), where the three new `override` subcommands were added. A user reading the command list sees no fsm entry.

findings.note: handleOverride hand-rolls flag parsing instead of using the file's own flagValue helper (main.go:467), so a value-less trailing flag is silently dropped rather than rejected. `metareview override request F1 --reason` leaves reason empty and exits 1 with 'override request needs a reason of at least 12 characters' instead of the CLI-wide exit-2 'Missing value for --reason'. Same for --by and --escalation; a `--reason --by` sequence also silently captures '--by' as the reason, where flagValue rejects a --prefixed value.

evidence.note: case --reason only assigns when i+1 < len(args), no else branch
flagValue exits 2 on a missing or --prefixed value everywhere else in main.go

findings.note: `override list --pending` prints nothing at all when override records exist but none are pending: the 'no process overrides recorded' line at main.go:526 is gated on len(records)==0, i.e. no overrides of any status. The CI-facing invocation therefore succeeds with empty stdout, which is indistinguishable from a command that did not run.

evidence.note: empty-state message keyed off total records, not the filtered set
pending>0 path prints to stderr and exits 1; the zero-pending path prints nothing

findings.note: defaultActor() collapses every git failure (git absent, not a repo, user.email unset) into an empty string, so the user is told 'override request needs an actor (--by)' with no indication that identity lookup failed. Given the doc's emphasis that --by is audit metadata, a distinguishable message would help.

evidence.note: err from git config is discarded and "" returned
RequestOverride rejects an empty actor with a message that only mentions --by

findings.note: mustResultFile os.ReadFile's an explicit --shard-result path with no size cap, while the ingestion path deliberately ignores result files over 256 KiB (see docs/tasks/pr-b-shard-ingestion.md slice 1). A pathological --shard-result is fully read into memory before ParseResult can reject it. Bounded by the fact that the path is operator-supplied, hence low.
